title: Level 1 Spanish — Unit 01: Polite Greetings & Language Barriers
description: Learn to get a local's attention politely in San Juan, ask if they understand English, and express that you speak a little Spanish.

steps.npcLine: [You see a woman walking down the street in San Juan and want to get her attention politely]
steps.npcTranslation: Goal: Excuse yourself politely to get her attention.
steps.userTask: Say politely: 'Excuse me, miss.'

options.reason: 'Mujer' is unnatural and overly direct when getting a stranger's attention. Use 'señorita'.
'La dama' translates to 'the lady' which is not used as a direct greeting.
'Oye, chica' ('Hey, girl') is overly casual for a first interaction.

steps.npcLine: Sí, diga. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
steps.npcTranslation: Yes, tell me. How can I help you?
steps.userTask: Ask her: 'Do you understand English?'

options.reason: Literal translation error. Use 'entiende inglés' or 'habla inglés'.
Mixing polite 'usted' with informal 'tú' verb form is grammatically inconsistent.
Unnatural phrasing. Native speakers ask '¿Entiende inglés?'

steps.npcLine: No, lo siento. No hablo inglés. ¿Y usted?
steps.npcTranslation: No, I'm sorry. I don't speak English. And you?
steps.userTask: Respond: 'I understand a little Spanish.'
acceptableVariations: Yo entiendo un poco de español

options.reason: 'Pequeño' means small in physical size. Use 'un poco de' for amounts.
'Tener' means to possess objects. Languages use 'entender' or 'hablar'.
'Corto' means short in length. Say 'entiendo un poco'.

title: Level 1 Spanish — Unit 02: Asking Directions & Finding Locations
description: Practice asking a passerby where the main plaza or hotel is located in Madrid.

steps.npcLine: [You are standing in Madrid and need to find the Plaza Mayor]
steps.npcTranslation: Goal: Ask a passerby politely where the plaza is.
steps.userTask: Ask politely: 'Excuse me, where is the Plaza Mayor?'
acceptableVariations: Disculpe donde esta la Plaza Mayor

options.reason: Physical location of places uses 'estar' ('está'), not 'ser'.
Unnatural. Use '¿dónde está...?' to ask for locations.
Commanding phrasing. Ask politely with '¿dónde está...?'

steps.npcLine: La Plaza Mayor está muy cerca, a dos cuadras a la derecha.
steps.npcTranslation: Plaza Mayor is very close, two blocks to the right.
steps.userTask: Confirm: 'Is it to the right?'

options.reason: Literal translation of 'right hand side'. In Spanish say 'a la derecha'.
'Recta' means straight line. 'Right direction' is 'la derecha'.
'Al derecho' means right-side up. Use 'a la derecha'.

steps.npcLine: Sí, exactamente. Camine dos cuadras y la verá.
steps.npcTranslation: Yes, exactly. Walk two blocks and you will see it.
steps.userTask: Thank him warmly: 'Thank you very much, sir. Have a good day!'

options.reason: 'Tenga gracias' is invalid. Say 'muchas gracias'.
Do not translate 'big thanks' literally. Use 'muchas gracias'.
'De nada' means 'you're welcome'! Use 'muchas gracias'.

title: Level 1 Spanish — Unit 03: Ordering Food & Drinks at a Café
description: Order coffee and empanadas in Mexico City, ask for the bill, and thank the server.

steps.npcLine: [You are sitting at a café in Mexico City and the waiter approaches]
steps.npcTranslation: Goal: Order a coffee with milk and bottled water.
steps.userTask: Say: 'I would like a coffee with milk and a water, please.'
steps.expectedResponse: Quisiera un café con leche y un agua, por favor
acceptableVariations: Quisiera un cafe con leche y agua por favor
Quiero un café con leche y agua, por favor
Un café con leche y un agua, por favor

options.text: Quisiera un café con leche y un agua, por favor
Yo quiero beber agua y café blanco
options.reason: Coffee with milk is 'café con leche', not 'café blanco'.

options.text: Dame un café y agua rápida
options.reason: 'Dame' ('give me') without 'por favor' sounds demanding.

options.text: Me gustaría un café con crema
options.reason: Spanish cafés use milk ('leche'), not heavy cream ('crema').

steps.npcLine: Muy bien. ¿Desea algo de comer también?
steps.npcTranslation: Very well. Would you like something to eat as well?
steps.userTask: Order: 'Yes, two chicken empanadas, please.'
steps.expectedResponse: Sí, dos empanadas de pollo, por favor
acceptableVariations: Si dos empanadas de pollo por favor

options.text: Sí, dos empanadas de pollo, por favor

options.reason: Adjectives follow nouns in Spanish: 'empanadas de pollo'.
Empanadas are pastries, not plain bread ('pan').
'Emparedado' is a sandwich, not an empanada.

steps.npcLine: Enseguida se lo traigo.
steps.npcTranslation: I'll bring it right away.
steps.userTask: Ask for the bill: 'Excuse me, the check please.'

options.reason: 'Cheque' is a banking check, not a restaurant bill ('la cuenta').
Unnatural. To ask for the bill, say 'la cuenta, por favor'.
Literal translation trap. Natives always ask for 'la cuenta'.

title: Level 1 Spanish — Unit 04: Shopping at a Local Market
description: Buy fresh apples and oranges at a market stand in Bogota and ask for the price.

steps.npcLine: [You approach a fruit vendor at the Paloquemao market in Bogota]
steps.npcTranslation: Goal: Greet the vendor politely.
steps.userTask: Say: 'Good morning! How much are the apples?'
acceptableVariations: Buenos dias cuanto cuestan las manzanas

options.reason: Grammatically incorrect. Use '¿cuánto cuestan...?'
Commanding phrasing. Ask politely with '¿cuánto cuestan...?'
Imprecise. Name the specific fruit: 'las manzanas'.

steps.npcLine: Las manzanas cuestan dos mil pesos el kilo. ¿Desea también naranjas?
steps.npcTranslation: Apples cost two thousand pesos a kilo. Would you also like oranges?
steps.userTask: Respond: 'Yes, I would like one kilo of oranges too.'
steps.expectedResponse: Sí, quisiera un kilo de naranjas también
acceptableVariations: Si quisiera un kilo de naranjas tambien
Sí, un kilo de naranjas, por favor

options.text: Sí, quisiera un kilo de naranjas también
Sí, dame un kilo de anaranjado
options.reason: 'Anaranjado' is the color orange. The fruit is 'la naranja'.

options.text: Sí, yo tomo la fruta naranja
options.reason: Unnatural. Use 'quisiera' or 'quiero' when ordering.
Saying 'I want to eat' sounds awkward when purchasing groceries.

steps.npcLine: Aquí tiene todo. Son cinco mil pesos en total.
steps.npcTranslation: Here you go. That's five thousand pesos in total.
steps.userTask: Pay the vendor: 'Here you go. Thank you very much!'

options.reason: 'Toma tu dinero' ('take your money') sounds blunt.
Literal translation of 'it's all yours'. Say 'aquí tiene'.
'De nada' means 'you're welcome'. Say 'muchas gracias'.

title: Level 1 Spanish — Unit 05: Taking a Taxi in Buenos Aires
description: Tell a taxi driver your destination and ask for the fare.

steps.npcLine: [You get into a taxi outside your hotel in Buenos Aires]
steps.npcTranslation: Goal: Tell the driver where you want to go.
steps.userTask: Say: 'Hello! To the airport, please.'

options.reason: Literal translation trap. Airport is 'el aeropuerto'.
'Avión' is the airplane itself! Say 'al aeropuerto'.
Unnatural. State destination simply: 'al aeropuerto, por favor'.

steps.npcLine: Perfecto, vamos para allá. Hay un poco de tráfico.
steps.npcTranslation: Perfect, let me head there. There is a bit of traffic.
steps.userTask: Ask the driver: 'How much is the fare approximately?'

options.reason: Unnatural. Ask '¿cuánto cuesta el viaje?'
Grammatically awkward. Use '¿cuánto cuesta...?'
'Is your car cheap?' does not ask for the fare.

steps.npcLine: Serán unos cuatro mil pesos. Ya estamos llegando.
steps.npcTranslation: It will be about four thousand pesos. We are arriving now.
steps.userTask: Thank the driver: 'Great, here is the money. Thank you!'
acceptableVariations: Excelente aqui esta el dinero gracias

options.reason: Too abrupt for polite customer interaction.
'De nada' means 'you're welcome'. Say 'gracias'.
Irrelevant phrase. Hand over payment with 'aquí está'.
